meaning: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome. A long-term, multi-system illness. See [What is ME/CFS?](/understanding/)
The delayed crash after doing more than your body can manage. The hallmark of ME/CFS. See [Symptoms](/understanding/symptoms/#post-exertional-malaise-in-detail).
Managing activity to stay inside your energy limits and avoid PEM. See [Pacing](/living/pacing/).
The amount of activity you can do without triggering PEM. It changes over time.
Overdoing it on good days, then crashing. The most common path to getting worse.
Ongoing symptoms after COVID-19. Many people with Long COVID meet ME/CFS criteria.
Symptoms that worsen when upright and improve lying down.
Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Heart rate rises by 30+ beats per minute on standing. See [POTS](/living/orthostatic-intolerance/).
Reduced blood flow to the brain when upright, caused by breathing out too much carbon dioxide. It can happen without a racing heart.
The automatic part of the nervous system that controls heart rate, blood pressure, digestion and temperature.
Any malfunction of the autonomic nervous system. POTS is one type.
Inflammation in the brain or nervous system.
The brain's waste-clearance system, which works mostly during sleep. Found to be impaired in ME/CFS in 2026.
The "energy factories" inside cells that make ATP using oxygen.
The cell's energy currency.
The inefficient backup way cells make energy without enough oxygen, producing lactate. Tips in too early in ME/CFS.
Electron carriers needed for energy production. NADH is also a supplement.
Nicotinamide mononucleotide / nicotinamide riboside. Supplements the body converts into NAD⁺.
Coenzyme Q10, part of the energy-production chain. Ubiquinol is its active form.
Acetyl-L-carnitine. Helps carry fuel into mitochondria.
Dimethylglycine. An ingredient in some supplement blends.
A calcium ion channel that Griffith University found doesn't work properly on immune cells in ME/CFS.
Natural killer cells, immune cells that fight viruses.
Antibodies that target the body's own tissues. Found in some people with ME/CFS.
A blood-filtering procedure that removes antibodies.
A protein targeted in PET scans to show immune activity or energy changes.
The protective lining that controls what passes from blood into the brain.
The virus that causes glandular fever. A common ME/CFS trigger. It stays in the body and can reactivate.
A related herpes-family virus that can also reactivate.
EBV antibody tests. IgM suggests recent or active infection; IgG shows past exposure.
EBV nuclear antigen antibody. Appears months after infection and helps date it.
EBV early antigen antibody. Rises when EBV reactivates.
Lactate dehydrogenase, an enzyme that leaks from stressed cells. See [Tests](/treatment/testing/#ld-lactate-dehydrogenase).
The five forms of LD (LD1–LD5). The mix shows which tissue it came from.
Creatine kinase, a marker of muscle damage.
Blood markers of general inflammation. Usually very low in ME/CFS.
A measure of your iron stores.
A blood marker that rises if you're functionally short of B12 or folate.
A blood marker of mast cell activity (allergic-type reactions).
The variation between heartbeats. A drop can warn of a crash 1–2 days ahead.
Apnoea-hypopnoea index. Breathing events per hour in a sleep study.
Obstructive sleep apnoea.
Continuous positive airway pressure. A machine that keeps the airway open during sleep.
Low-dose naltrexone. See [Medications](/treatment/medications/#low-dose-naltrexone-ldn).
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Breathing oxygen in a pressurised chamber.
Intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia therapy. Breathing air that alternates between low and high oxygen.

Graded exercise therapy. Increasing exercise on a set schedule. No longer recommended by NICE or the CDC for ME/CFS; its evidence is disputed. See [the debate about GET](/treatment/avoid/#the-debate-about-graded-exercise-therapy).
Cognitive behavioural therapy. Can support coping, but isn't a cure for ME/CFS.
Canadian Consensus Criteria, a diagnostic definition often used in trials.
International Consensus Criteria, a stricter diagnostic definition.
The 2015 US Institute of Medicine (now National Academy of Medicine) diagnostic criteria.
An older, broad definition of CFS that doesn't require PEM.
A 0–100 disability scale used in ME/CFS. Lower means more disabled.
Randomised controlled trial. The strongest kind of evidence.
A dummy treatment used for comparison. In ME/CFS, 20–40%+ of people feel better on placebo.
A study where everyone knows what treatment they're getting. There's no placebo, so results are less reliable.
Using an approved drug for a condition it isn't officially approved for.
A measurable sign of disease, like a blood test result.
Influenced by many genes, each with a small effect.
Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry.
National Centre for Neuroimmunology and Emerging Diseases, Griffith University.
Therapeutic Goods Administration, Australia's medicines regulator.
National Health and Medical Research Council, Australia's main medical research funder.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (UK). Its 2021 ME/CFS guideline rejected GET.
Occupational therapist. Helps with pacing, energy management and daily living.
